subject: Intermittent 5xx/429 Surge - Dedicated VPC Peering Churn (FinGuard)
messages:
From: Sara Khan <sara.khan@finguard.com>
To: jonas_weber@redwood.ai
Date: 2027-03-23T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Spike in 5xx/429 from our Dedicated pool - urgent

Jonas,

We're seeing a sudden surge of 5xx and 429 responses from requests routed through the dedicated pool attached to our VPC peering. Errors started ~08:45 PDT and have been intermittent since. Impact: checkout timeouts for ~7% of user requests, visible in our GA and internal logs.

Attached one pcap capture from our app box hitting the Redwood endpoint (net-trace-20270323.pcap). We also have a short traceroute. Key observations from ops: many connections show RST or TCP retransmits during attempts to reach the inference endpoint; some flows are succeeding briefly then failing.

Please escalate to your network/infra team — this is a high-severity outage for our production traffic. We're also preparing a support ticket on our side (ticket #FG-7421).

-Sara
Sara Khan
CTO, FinGuard

[attachment: net-trace-20270323.pcap (PCAP, 2.3MB)]

From: jonas_weber@redwood.ai
To: Sara Khan <sara.khan@finguard.com>, FinGuard Ops <ops@finguard.com>
Cc: monica_patel@redwood.ai, rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai, laura_bennett@redwood.ai
Date: 2027-03-23T09:25:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Spike in 5xx/429 from our Dedicated pool - urgent

Sara — thanks for the heads up and the pcap. I've looped in Monica (CS), Rishi (infra), and Laura (networking) to triage immediately.

Quick acknowledgment:
- We're treating this as a P1 and have opened an internal incident (PagerDuty PDR-8421).
- Initial questions for ops: can you confirm whether the impacted flows are all from the same region and whether traffic is using the dedicated NAT gateway we set up? Any NAT gateway logs would help (source ports, ephemeral exhaustion).

Working hypothesis: we've seen similar signatures where VPC peering + provider NAT gateways exhibit port churn / asymmetric routing causing ephemeral port exhaustion and connection resets under heavy concurrent connections. We'll validate with packet captures and host traceroutes.

Action items I just triggered:
- Rishi to pull gateway counters and NAT metrics, check for port exhaustion and socket limits.
- Laura to run targeted traceroutes and BGP/peering checks from both sides.
- Monica to coordinate weekly exec updates and procurement if there's an SLA/credit ask.

I'll update within 30 minutes with findings.

—Jonas
Jonas Weber
Sr. Account Exec, Redwood Inference

From: rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai
To: jonas_weber@redwood.ai, laura_bennett@redwood.ai, monica_patel@redwood.ai
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Date: 2027-03-23T09:47:00-07:00
Subject: RE: Spike in 5xx/429 from our Dedicated pool - urgent

Initial triage notes (summary of checks done at 09:47):
- NAT gateway metrics: temporary spike in concurrent mappings on the customer's NAT | 95th percentile ephemeral usage rose sharply between 08:40-08:55. No clear sustained flag for port exhaustion yet but correlation is strong.
- Firewall logs: increased connection resets logged at the edge of our dedicated overlay; some flows show SYN then immediate RST from provider transit.
- DNS: customer TTLs are low (30s); we saw a flurry of re-resolves which could amplify short-lived connection churn.
- BGP/peering: no control-plane flap in provider console, but dataplane path asymmetry noted — packets forwarded to different egress IPs intermittently.

Hypothesis: a combination of transient NAT port pressure on the peering/NAT hop + DNS churn is causing many clients to quickly re-open connections without proper backoff, generating retry storms and exposing 5xx/429 token-throttle points in our fronting proxies.

Next technical steps:
1) Collect complete traceroute matrix from 3 customer hosts (attached traceroutes-3hosts.txt).
2) Ask provider to surface NAT allocation table for the affected window.
3) Temporarily enable more permissive keepalive and connection re-use settings in the dedicated pool (can be rolled back).
4) Deploy short-term rate limiting adjustment to reduce token-throttle 429s and avoid cascades.

I've attached a short dump of traceroutes. Will follow with provider logs within the hour.

- Rishi
Principal Infra Engineer, Redwood Inference

[attachment: traceroutes-3hosts.txt]

From: laura_bennett@redwood.ai
To: jonas_weber@redwood.ai, rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai, monica_patel@redwood.ai
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Date: 2027-03-23T11:05:00-07:00
Subject: RE: Spike in 5xx/429 from our Dedicated pool - urgent

Update after provider engagement (11:05):
- Provider confirmed they saw a short-lived NAT translation table rebuild in the customer's peering VLAN between 08:42-08:58 due to a control-plane restart on one of their edge boxes (they call it a "peering agent restart"). That caused ephemeral port remapping and a subset of flows to be dropped while translations re-established.
- They also flagged that FinGuard's application instances are opening many short-lived connections (short TTLs + no keepalives), which increases mapping churn on NAT devices.

Recommendation (immediate mitigation):
- Enable aggressive connection reuse on our side of the dedicated pool (reduce new socket creation). Rolling change across pool alpha nodes now; this will reduce new ephemeral allocation pressure.
- Ask FinGuard to increase client keepalive and backoff; Monica can coordinate that ask with Sara.
- Apply conservative rate-limit change so our fronting proxies return 429 with Retry-After instead of 5xx where possible to avoid token-throttle cascades.

I've drafted a one-page joint action plan and escalation brief; attaching as joint-action-plan-finguard.docx. Requesting Monica to schedule an executive sync (CRO + FinGuard CTO) after we confirm impact reduction.

- Laura
Network Lead, Redwood Inference

[attachment: joint-action-plan-finguard.docx]

From: monica_patel@redwood.ai
To: Sara Khan <sara.khan@finguard.com>, jonas_weber@redwood.ai, laura_bennett@redwood.ai, rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, sales_ops@redwood.ai, procurement@finguard.com
Date: 2027-03-24T14:05:00-07:00
Subject: Exec brief + next steps (FinGuard outage window 08:45-09:05 PDT)

Sara — thank you for the quick escalation and for the pcap/traces. Summary for execs:
- Impact window: 2027-03-23 08:45-09:05 PDT. Symptoms: elevated 5xx (internal proxy 502/504) and 429 token-throttle responses during retry storms; approximately 7% of checkout requests affected.
- Root cause (joint): provider peering agent restart caused ephemeral NAT translation rebuild; FinGuard client connection patterns (short TTL, high concurrency) amplified the effect.
- Mitigations performed: connection reuse enabled on dedicated pool; conservative proxy rate-limit deployed to return 429 with Retry-After; provider confirmed peering agent software patch queued.

Proposed immediate asks:
1) Request formal SLA credit for the 08:45-09:05 window (FinGuard procurement cc'd).
2) Agreed engineering changes: FinGuard to increase keepalive to 60s and implement exponential backoff on client retries; Redwood to keep the connection reuse change and monitor for 72h.
3) Follow-up: 48-hour joint post-incident review.

Sara, can you confirm acceptance of the action items so we can move the SLA/credit conversation to procurement? If you'd like, we can route a short executive 15-minute call with our CRO and your CTO later today.

Thanks — Monica
Monica Patel
Customer Success Lead, Redwood Inference
